ended: Lost the East 1st Round 3-4 to DET

archetype.name: Early Playoff Exit (blown 3-1 lead)
archetype.definition: A league-average team by margin that won enough to host a first-round series, led Detroit 3-1, then scored too little to close it.

report.headline: Orlando defended well enough to beat Detroit, then forgot how to score

recap.finish: 45-37, second in the Southeast; lost the East 1st Round 3-4 to DET after leading 3-1
recap.body:
This was a reshuffled version of Orlando rather than a step forward. For two years the Magic won with a top-two defense and a bottom-tier offense. In 2025-26 the offense climbed to 19th and the defense slipped to 11th. The net result was a Net Rtg of 0.6, 17th in the league: a middle-of-the-pack team that won 45 games, slightly ahead of the 43 its +52 differential implies. The first-round result also repeated recent history. Three playoff wins matched 2023-24, and that series ended in the first round too.

The season opened 2-4 in October. A 10-4 November followed, with most of the season's big run-of-form, and pushed the record to 12-8. Then came three months of near-.500 basketball (7-7, 6-7, 6-5) and a 9-8 March that left them 40-35. The season held both a 7-game winning streak and a 6-game losing streak. April was the best stretch since November. They went 4-1 over the last five at +10.2 a game, including a 123-107 win over Detroit. The 7-3 finish to the last ten flatters them, though. It carries a -11 differential because of a 139-87 loss at Toronto and a 130-101 home loss to Atlanta. They finished just behind Atlanta's 46-36 for the division.

Desmond Bane carried the team. He played all 82 games, scored 1,647 points on 60.7 TS %, led the roster with 7.4 Win Shares and ranked 7th of 144 on his tab, which put the backcourt at an A-. Jalen Suggs added a +7.6 On-Off in 57 games. In the frontcourt (B-), Paolo Banchero scored 1,599 points on a 27.6 USG %, but the team was slightly worse with him on the floor. Wendell Carter Jr. (61.7 TS %, 6.2 Win Shares) and Goga Bitadze (70 TS %, 2.8 BPM) did efficient work around him. The wings were the problem at C-, because Franz Wagner played only 34 games. By style, this was a team that got to the line, with FT Rate 2nd in the league, and cleaned the defensive glass, with DRB % 5th. It still couldn't shoot: 3P % was 27th and 3PA Rate 24th.

The series followed the season's identity. Orlando stole Game 1 in Detroit 112-101, lost Game 2 83-98, then held serve at home 113-105 and 94-88 to go up 3-1. After that the offense failed. They lost 109-116 in Game 5, scored 79 at home in Game 6 and lost Game 7 94-116. The defense was not the issue: opponents' eFG % of 49.9 ranked 2nd among 16 playoff teams. Orlando's own 46.4 eFG % ranked last. Banchero was good, with 184 points and a 6.5 BPM on a 31.8 USG %. Franz Wagner played only 4 of the 7 games but posted a +22.3 On-Off, and Jamal Cain absorbed 123 wing minutes at a -4 BPM. Suggs shot a 41.9 TS %.

The lesson is the same one the last few seasons have taught. A team this short on shooting needs its defense to be elite and its few creators to be healthy. This year it had neither for long enough.

highlights.title: Bane's durable, efficient lead role
highlights.body: Bane played every game, scored efficiently and produced the most Win Shares on the team, and he is the main reason the backcourt graded A-. His efficiency came with moderate usage, so it does not look like a hot-shooting fluke. He was also the steadiest scorer in the playoffs, so this should carry over.

highlights.title: Offense finally reached the middle
highlights.body: After finishing 27th the year before, the offense rose to 19th. Almost all of that came from getting to the line and from interior efficiency, since the shooting stayed poor. Its FT Rate ranked 2nd, and Carter Jr. and Bitadze both finished well above the league's TS %. It is a real gain, but it rests on free throws and big men rather than on spacing.

highlights.title: Playoff defense was title-caliber
highlights.body: Detroit's eFG % against Orlando ranked 2nd-lowest among playoff teams, and the Magic forced turnovers at the 3rd-best rate. That is the identity of the 2023-24 and 2024-25 teams showing up when it mattered. It suggests the regular-season slide to 11th on defense is recoverable.

lowlights.title: The offense died with the series in hand
lowlights.body: Up 3-1, Orlando lost three straight and scored 79 and 94 in the final two games. Its playoff eFG % ranked last of 16. Suggs shot a 41.9 TS %, and with Franz Wagner limited, the wing minutes went to players who couldn't score.

lowlights.title: Still can't shoot threes
lowlights.body: 3P % ranked 27th, and the team took fewer threes than most. This is not new: the 3P % was 31.8 last season and below 35 in four of the five seasons before. It caps the offense, and it is why the scoring dried up against a set defense.

lowlights.title: A thin, banged-up wing group
lowlights.body: Franz Wagner played 34 games, and the wings graded C-, the roster's weakest group. The defense showed the hole too: it allowed the 24th-most points to small forwards. When Wagner played in the playoffs, Orlando was much better.

arc.note: A hot November gave way to three months of .500 ball, and a strong April run carried into a 3-1 series lead. Then three straight losses ended it.

recap.nextYear: The foundation is Bane, plus efficient big-man play from Carter Jr. and Bitadze, and a defense that proved in the playoffs it can still be elite. Banchero's playoff line was the strongest on the team, but his regular-season On-Off was negative, so how his high usage fits remains an open question. The fixes the numbers point to are clear. A healthy, productive wing group matters most, given the C- grade and Franz Wagner's 34 games. Shooting has been bottom-tier for years. The record was close to honest: two wins above what the margin implies is mild luck, so this roster as it stood was a mid-40s-win, roughly .500-by-margin team.

confidence.note: Full 82 games and a seven-game series; the sheet doesn't explain Wagner's absences.
